purpose: What the apprentice must learn from the expert to fly a high-voltage line inspection alone. Each task has slots; a slot is filled with a reusable rule (condition -> action -> reason, with a threshold or cue when relevant), never with a one-off anecdote. Telemetry already measures distances, speeds and heights: do not ask for them, use them as evidence and ask for the rule, the threshold, the cue, the condition or the abort criterion behind them. Slots listing 'evidence' are checked against the telemetry of later flights: the same behaviour confirms the rule, a different one makes the apprentice ask what changed.

slot_types.threshold: a limit or target value and why (how close, how slow, how high)
slot_types.procedure: the order or pattern of actions
slot_types.cue: what the pilot looks at or notices to decide
slot_types.condition: when the pilot does it differently (wind, defect, interference, traffic)
slot_types.abort: what makes the pilot stop, back off or abandon
slot_types.assessment: how the pilot judges severity or what gets reported

evidence_metrics.cable_dist_median: typical distance to the nearest cable (m)
evidence_metrics.cable_dz_median: typical height relative to the nearest cable (m, positive = above)
evidence_metrics.tree_dist_min: closest distance to the nearest tree (m)

tasks.name: Pre-flight checks, take-off and overview
tasks.detect: from take-off until the drone first comes within 10 m of a tower or 6 m of a cable
measured: altitude reached before the first approach

slots.label: Go / no-go
slots.learn: Weather and wind limits for flying at all; what is checked before take-off
slots.ask_example: Before you take off, what wind or weather would make you not fly near the line?

slots.label: Route plan
slots.learn: Order of pylons and spans, which side of the line to work from, and why
slots.ask_example: How do you decide which pylon to start with and which side of the line to work from?

slots.label: Overview climb
slots.learn: Whether and how high to climb for an overview of the structure before going close, and what is checked from there
slots.ask_example: When you climb above the line first, what are you checking from up there before going closer?

tasks.name: Transit along the line between structures
tasks.detect: moving faster than 1.5 m/s within 20 m of the cables, near nothing else

slots.label: Transit position
slots.learn: Where to fly when moving along the line: above or beside the cables, never between them, and the offset kept
slots.ask_example: When you move along the line, what is your rule for where to be relative to the cables?

slots.label: Transit speed
slots.learn: Speed limits when travelling near the line and where to slow down
slots.ask_example: How fast do you allow yourself to travel near the line, and where do you start slowing down?

slots.label: Following the sag
slots.learn: How the cable sag between pylons changes the flight height
slots.ask_example: How do you deal with the cable dipping between pylons when you follow it?

tasks.name: Approach to a pylon
tasks.detect: within 10 m of a tower and not moving away from it, not hovering at an insulator

slots.label: Approach path
slots.learn: Direction, height and speed of the final approach to a tower, and where to stop first
slots.ask_example: When you come up to a tower, from which direction and height do you like to arrive, and why?

slots.label: Tower check
slots.learn: What is checked on the tower itself: lean, bent members, corrosion, missing bolts, bird nests on the crossarm
slots.ask_example: When you first look at a tower, what tells you the structure itself has a problem?

slots.label: Tower clearance
slots.learn: Minimum distance kept from the tower body and crossarm
slots.ask_example: What is the closest you will go to the tower or crossarm, and what decides that distance?

tasks.name: Close inspection of an insulator string
tasks.detect: slower than 1 m/s within 7 m of an insulator

slots.label: Viewpoints
slots.learn: Which viewpoints are needed for a complete check (top attachment at the crossarm, the discs, the bottom clamp on the cable) and from which side or height
slots.ask_example: To inspect an insulator string completely, which views do you need, and in what order?

slots.label: Inspection distance
slots.learn: Distance kept from the string while inspecting, and what limits going closer
slots.ask_example: What distance do you aim for when you inspect a string, and what stops you going closer?

slots.label: Defect cues
slots.learn: How each insulator defect is recognised: broken or shattered disc, flashover soot, pollution coating, cracks
slots.ask_example: What exactly do you look for on the discs to tell a damaged insulator from a healthy one?

slots.label: Hold time
slots.learn: How long to hold and how stable the drone must be before the inspection counts
slots.ask_example: How long do you hold in front of a string, and what makes you decide it is enough?

tasks.name: Inspection of the conductors along a span
tasks.detect: within 6 m of a cable, not at an insulator or tower

slots.label: Scan technique
slots.learn: Offset, speed and viewing angle while scanning a cable, and whether both sides are checked
slots.ask_example: When you scan a cable along the span, how do you position yourself so you do not miss anything?

slots.label: Cable damage cues
slots.learn: How conductor problems are recognised: broken or birdcaged strands, foreign objects such as a kite, damaged dampers, spacers or splices
slots.ask_example: What does a damaged conductor look like from the drone, and where along the span does it usually happen?

slots.label: Closer-look trigger
slots.learn: What makes the pilot stop, go closer or circle around a section of cable
slots.ask_example: What makes you stop and go around a section of cable instead of carrying on?

tasks.name: Confirming, rating and reporting a defect
tasks.detect: side task, active alongside the main one for 20 s after a defect_spotted event
measured: angles and distances used around the component

slots.label: Confirming a defect
slots.learn: How a suspected defect is confirmed (extra angles, distance, light) before it is reported
slots.ask_example: When you think you have spotted a defect, what do you do to be sure before reporting it?

slots.label: Severity
slots.learn: How severity is judged (repair immediately, within months, or monitor) for each defect type
slots.ask_example: How serious is this kind of defect for you: fix now, plan a repair, or just monitor?

slots.label: Report content
slots.learn: What must be recorded: location (pylon, span, phase, disc), component, views or photos, recommended action
slots.ask_example: If you reported this defect, what would the report need to contain for the repair crew?

tasks.name: Flying with electromagnetic interference and wind
tasks.detect: side task, active alongside the main one: compass interference above 0.3, or wind above 5 m/s within 8 m of a cable
measured: side of the cable relative to the wind

slots.label: Interference response
slots.learn: How compass interference is noticed near the cables and what the pilot does (yaw correction, more distance, slower, manual flying)
slots.ask_example: Close to the cable the heading starts to wander: how do you notice it and what do you do?

slots.label: Interference distance
slots.learn: Distance kept from energised conductors because of interference
slots.ask_example: Because of the interference near the conductors, what distance do you keep as your own limit?

slots.label: Wind side
slots.learn: Which side of a cable or structure to work from in wind, and extra margin taken in gusts
slots.ask_example: With this wind, which side of the cable do you prefer to work from, and how much margin do you add in gusts?

tasks.name: Crossing a road
tasks.detect: within 8 m of the road (including a pause to check the traffic) or over it

slots.label: Crossing rule
slots.learn: How a road is crossed: height, crossing straight and quickly, never hovering above traffic
slots.ask_example: What is your rule for crossing a road with the drone?

slots.label: Traffic check
slots.learn: What is checked before and while crossing, and when the pilot waits or goes around
slots.ask_example: What do you check before you cross, and what would make you wait?

slots.label: Tree clearance
slots.learn: Distance the drone keeps from trees and how the pilot passes them
slots.ask_example: How much room do you give a tree when you fly past it, and why that much?

slots.label: Tree risk check
slots.learn: How vegetation is judged as a risk to the line (distance to the conductor, growth towards it, fall-in risk) and when it is reported
slots.ask_example: When you look at a tree near the line, what tells you it needs to be reported for trimming?

tasks.name: Abort and emergency handling
tasks.detect: the 4 s after a very_close_cable or collision event

slots.label: Abort triggers
slots.learn: What makes the pilot abort an inspection: control problems, interference, gusts, low battery, losing sight of the drone
slots.ask_example: What would make you abandon an inspection and pull away from the line?

slots.label: Escape manoeuvre
slots.learn: The immediate escape manoeuvre: which direction, climb or back off, and why
slots.ask_example: If something goes wrong near the cable, what is your first move to get clear?

slots.label: Return & landing
slots.learn: Return path, height and battery reserve for coming home without crossing the line
slots.ask_example: How do you plan the way home so you never have to cross the line low on battery?

industry_reference.note: Published values vary widely between sources and utilities; the expert's own rule is what the apprentice learns. Use these only to recognise plausible answers and to ask sharper follow-ups.
industry_reference.standoff_energised_lines: about 3 to 9 m (10 to 30 ft) minimum for close work, set by utility protocol; magnetic fields above about 180 microtesla made test UAVs drift towards the line
industry_reference.corridor_flight: fly above or beside the line, not between conductors; some guides keep 30 to 45 m horizontal and 15 m vertical for general flight
industry_reference.insulator_views: about three viewpoints per insulator string: the attachment point at each end and the string itself; each tower head also needs a view of the shield wire attachment
industry_reference.defect_priority: one utility scale: priority 1 = immediate action, priority 2 = within 12 months (6 in high fire-risk areas), priority 3 = within 60 months
industry_reference.road_crossing: no sustained flight over moving vehicles; the pilot chooses a safe way to cross an active road
industry_reference.typical_defects: broken or flashed-over insulators, pollution on insulators, broken conductor strands, hot connections and splices, corrosion and missing bolts on towers, loose or missing vibration dampers and spacers, bird nests and foreign objects, vegetation encroachment, tower lean or bent members
